summary: Bath County tower on Warm Springs Mountain, built 1934 by the CCC for Virginia forestry; now in a Nature Conservancy preserve, not staffed, public route unclear.

visit.trail_note: The May 10, 2018 visit report describes a fire road up from a red gate off Airport Road. The preserve lists three public trails (Ingalls Overlook, Sandy Gap, Bear Loop) but does not say whether the public may reach the tower. Ask the Conservancy before going.

events.note: Built by the CCC for the Virginia Department of Forestry on a state-owned easement from the Hot Springs Company
Coast and Geodetic Survey station recovery note places the fire tower on the highest part of the knob
Register visit May 10, 2018: good condition, not staffed, NHLR sign posted

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register lists The Nature Conservancy as administrator of the tower within its Warm Springs Mountain Preserve. The Weebly page names the Virginia Department of Forestry, which the Register says built it. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: The brief had no height. The 35-foot figure is the Register's, converted to 10.7 m. No source states that the public may drive or walk to the tower, so the record gives no access level; the public trails listed are the preserve's, not the tower's. The latest condition record is the May 2018 visit report. The Register has a photo path (nhlr.org /images/Lookout_Photos/US907_Bald_Knob/Scholetzky1.jpg) but no licence is stated, so no photo is added.
